title: Derived Hom from a bounded-above projective complex
statement: Let R be a ring and regard it as the structure ring of the one-point ringed site, with derived category D(R) defined by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let P^\bullet be a bounded-above cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] of projective R-modules [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], and let L^\bullet be a bounded-below cochain complex of R-modules. Then the ordinary Hom complex Hom_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,L^\bullet), whose degree-n term is \prod_p Hom_R(P^p,L^{p+n}), represents the derived Hom R Hom_R(P^\bullet,L^\bullet) obtained by specializing [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to this one-point ringed site. In particular its cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 0GM8, lemma-stalk-internal-hom, case (2), together with the K-projective construction of derived Hom

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution L^\bullet\to I^\bullet of the bounded-below complex L^\bullet in the one-point specialization of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Since P^\bullet is bounded above with projective terms, [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] says that Hom_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,-) sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms (apply its acyclicity assertion to the mapping cone). Hence Hom_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,L^\bullet)\to Hom_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,I^\bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism, and the latter is the representative used by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; therefore the ordinary Hom complex represents the derived Hom in D(R).

source.place: Tag 0GM8, lemma-stalk-internal-hom, case (2), using the K-projective replacement construction of Derived Categories Tag 06XR

proof.text: For the vanishing assertion, choose integers b and a with P^p=0 for p>b and L^q=0 for q<a. By the Hom-complex formula in the one-point specialization of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], its degree-n term is the product over p of Hom_R(P^p,L^{p+n}). A nonzero factor requires p\le b and p+n\ge a, so no factor exists when n<a-b; the product is then zero. Thus the cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees.
